item.description:

Journal of Materials Chemistry A | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in fluorine-terminated vacancy-ordered i-MXene/graphene heterostructures enabling aqueous lithium-ion batteries without costly, slow superconcentrated electrolytes. Significance: this design widens the water stability window via electrode engineering rather than water-in-salt electrolytes, offering a safer, lower-cost, faster-charging alternative and advancing practical aqueous battery anodes.
🏷 aqueous lithium-ion battery · i-MXene · graphene heterostructure · fluorine termination · vacancy ordering

Journal of Materials Chemistry A | ⭐ Review
💡 The novelty lies in using plasma to generate reactive anion species that precisely tailor lithium-battery interfaces, moving beyond conventional material modification.
